claims.claim_text: The current era is characterized by intense capitalist crises, including environmental destruction, stagnating wages, rising costs for workers, rapid displacement, violent police management of Black and brown people, brutal objectification of feminized workers, excessive working hours for those on salary, high levels of debt, an explosion of mental health problems, everyday social isolation, and an anti-democratic radical right bent on establishing minority rule.
Some time ago, the working class maintained solidarities based in the factory, in the neighborhood, and in common ways of life.
Working-class solidarities based in factories, neighborhoods, and shared ways of life provided access to collectively shared life essentials.
Collective access to essentials protected the working class from unpredictable changes in the market, such as housing insecurity or rising expenses.
Decades of counter-revolution have destroyed most working-class solidarities based in factories, neighborhoods, and shared ways of life.
The working class has been turned into isolated individuals.
The working class is left with few organic connections between its members.
The destruction of working-class solidarities and organic connections forces the working class to rely on the capitalist market for almost everything.
The ongoing crisis of capitalism now makes itself appear in every facet of life, and the working class is more market-dependent than ever.
The Communist Caucus describes the current era as seeming apocalyptic while capitalism seems indestructible.
